Cape Town’s Illegal Street Racing

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Join us as we dive into Cape Town’s underground world of illegal street racing and the elite Ghost Squad’s relentless pursuit to bring these speedsters to justice.

Unique Selling Point:
This story highlights the daring operations of the Ghost Squad, a covert unit within Cape Town’s Metro Police, dedicated to curbing the rampant street racing epidemic that endangers lives. The squad's efforts showcase a crucial fight for public safety against a deeply embedded culture of speed.

Summary:
Cape Town has become a hotspot for illegal street racing, a dangerous pastime that has led to countless accidents, fatalities, and a growing public safety concern. The Ghost Squad, an elite division of the Cape Town Metro Police, was formed to combat this threat. Operating with unmarked vehicles and covert tactics, the squad has become the frontline in a battle against street racers who show little regard for the law or human life.

This episode will explore the origins of illegal street racing in Cape Town, delving into the thrill-seeking culture that drives it. We'll follow the Ghost Squad on their night patrols, capturing their high-adrenaline confrontations with racers and offering viewers an inside look at the challenges they face in maintaining order on the city’s roads.

Further information:
Our story will unfold in two parts: the first will introduce viewers to the world of illegal street racing, featuring interviews with participants and community members impacted by this reckless behavior. The second part will focus on the Ghost Squad’s operations, showcasing their tactics, challenges, and successes in apprehending offenders.

We will capture the intensity of street racing through real footage, reenactments, and first-hand accounts, contrasting it with the Ghost Squad’s dedication to restoring safety. The episode will also address the legal and social implications of street racing, questioning whether current measures are enough to curb the issue.
We will reference past incidents of street racing tragedies, emphasizing the urgent need for continued law enforcement efforts. Interviews with traffic safety experts will provide insights into potential solutions, while community members will voice their concerns and hopes for safer streets. The episode will conclude with a reflection on the ongoing struggle between thrill-seekers and the forces of law and order.

Extra Budget Items:
We will be shooting over 3 days in Cape Town. 3 days with a camera crew.

Script : Ghost Squad vs Street Racers



1.V/O: A dangerous game playing out on Cape Town's darkened streets.
[ street racing visuals]

2.V/O Illegal street racing: an adrenaline-fueled thrill for speed.

Upsound Mikayla racer CAMA0764 :02:36 I race because you know when you want to get things off your mind, you just take a drive ,you just flatfoot your car and you just let go.

3.V/O A covert police unit on the frontlines, taking on the racers in a high-speed game of cat and mouse.
[shots of ghost squad driving]
Upsound: Ghost Squad officer Boswell CAMA0567 0:36 Whenever we have operations and we do get the street racers I do what must be done.
[Dramatic fade to black after opening]


5.V/O Cape Town’s illegal racing network comes to life on weekend nights, attracting hundreds of spectators… Cars are driven at speeds of up to 200 km/h in drag races and stunts … Sometimes with deadly consequences.
[Breather]
6.VO But an elite Cape Town Metro Police Unit, known as the Ghost Squad is using high-performance cars and highly-trained drivers to tackle a recent surge in street racing.
[breather]

VO: We’re at the City’s Killarney track where legal races are being hosted. Past experience suggests some of these drivers will later join other thrill-seekers on the streets.

Link There’s a race that's happening,but its Legal. and those street racers need to go home.Tonight we’ve been just briefed by the Ghost squad,if we run into an illegal race there’ll likely be a high speed chase and possibly any arrest.

Link CAMA0542 :Okay, so we're at a meeting point somewhere in Cape Town and we've just been briefed by the Ghost Squad. These are the guys trying to clamp down on illegal street racing. And tonight, we're going to join them on patrol.

7.V/O The Ghost Squad doesn’t only target illegal races. Since its formation in 2009, it’s caught close to 8,000 traffic offenders each month. Patrolling at night, its officers focus on reckless drivers and red-light runners. Adrian Long is their principal inspector.

Upsound Govan 0:00 So how exactly does the Ghost Squad work?

Upsound Ghost Squad Chief Inspector Adrian Long CAMA0539 0:11 : The Ghost Squad is a Is a unit within traffic services that was formed to...basically do undercover work. The officers are in full uniform, the vehicles are unmarked and it's to create an illusion of an omnipresent which basically means that anybody using our roads within the city of Cape Town won't know if any vehicle in front, behind or to the side of them is a potential Ghost squad car with an officer in it.


9.V/O On this Friday night, the Ghost Squad’s conducting an intelligence-driven patrol, trying to close the net on illegal street racers. Social media chatter is being monitored while overhead a drone is on the lookout for signs of action.

[Driving shots to transition ]

Upsound Govan How many high-speed chases?

Upsound officer Boswell CAMA 0567 Many I can't count. Too many!

10.V/O I’m paired with Senior Inspector Claude Boswell, one of the Ghost Squad’s best officers and an original member. He’s known for exceptional driving skills.

Upsound Officer Boswell CAMA0577 (alone night) 00:00 I was on normal enforcement prior to 2009. I was on the highway unit. And when the Ghost Squad started, I was nominated to start with the Ghost Squad, then we started by having more teams because of the success rate that we had.

11 V/O The car we’re in is fitted with technology able to detect license plates linked to outstanding warrants.

[ Officer Boswell on the freeway]
Upsound Officer Boswell CAMA0577 01:26, To do this job is a calling. You must enjoy working with people and also you want to make a difference out there on the road. Because it's not for everybody, this job.

12 V/O It’s an unusually quiet Friday night—almost too quiet

[ Short chase sequence ,create excitement with pulsating music ]

13 V/O Then, the radio crackles to life. A bakkie speeds down the freeway unaware he’s been spotted…The chase is on.

14 V/O Eventually, the driver finally pulls over. He’s clearly been drinking.

Link Govan CAMA 0586 The driver is two times over the limit, and he was going over two-hundred kilometers per hour, officer Boswell needs to take him to the police station and check him in.

[Driving shots fade into others to illustrate elapsed time]

15.V/O It’s 2 a.m. and it seems the racers have caught onto the Ghost Squad’s presence. After hours spent checking the usual hotpots, the shift ends.

[ Transition shot please. ]

16V/O Racers intercept radio frequencies and use informants to stay ahead of the law.

17.V/O And they’re becoming bolder, as this video taken in broad daylight shows.



Upsound JP Smith interview CAMA0630 12:42 We are told on occasion
rewards were even issued to people for being able to successfully flee the Hhost squad.

18.V/O The City’s Mayoral Committee member for safety and security, JP Smith, is determined to tackle the problem. He’s introduced a raft of laws to tighten the net.

Upsound JP Smith CAMA0630 0:12in the last 100 days, we had 300 complaints of drag racing. The city by-law that deals with removing your number plates because that's the first defensive measure that an illegal drag racer will engage in.we've created a substantial penalty we impound for no number plates, for repeat offenders with no driver's license//spectating an illegal racing event is an offense in terms

[Bridging shot]

Link Govan CAMA 0742 : To understand what the Ghost Squad is up against , we’ve made contact with illegal racers and we’ve been invited to an undisclosed location to find out why they take the risks they do



Upsound Govan CAMA0764 03:43 how do illegal street races get organised?

Upsound Mikayla CAMA0764 .03:59 Basically a message you don't know where to get your number they'll be like hey I have a call I04:04What?04:14 On the streets? On the streets. And then? On a very empty road. Okay so you get the call out and then? And then you go. You cannot deny it. Because at the end of the day you know you fast. That person knows it's fast. It's all about dragging. 04:33It's not about that, it's for the fun, it's for the passion. But there are some guys that's just, listen, I wanna be better than you. And I am better than you, and I'm gonna show you. So that's where the call-outs start coming out. For 5,000, and you don't know who calls you out. Sometimes more.


Upsound Mikayla CAMA0764 14:08 [Govan] The people who've been killed by illegal street races. So you think... It's a deadly sport. Um, it... it... literally everything is a deadly sport if you think about it. If you know you are watching street racing, why are you also putting yourself in danger by standing in the middle of the road.

[breather /transition]
19V/ At high speeds, a single swerve can be fatal. We meet an enthusiast badly injured at an illegal race in July. Fearing arrest, she’s asked us to hide her identity.

Upsound Jean Jansen CAMA0002 00:00 My friends decided we're going to go and watch the drags in Atlantis. [Use cellphone visuals titled street racing from Jean Jansen]

Upsound Jean Jansen CAMA0002 00:29 The guystarted performing in the road, started doing donuts at the, where they start the races I was also standing on the side. He lost control of the car. And he basically went off road and the back of his vehicle knocked me.so I just remember the world is spinning around me

20.V/O Her injuries were severe.

Upsound Jean Jansen CAMA0002 I have a fractured pelvic bone and it also shifted up. But I am receiving physiotherapy for that. And then I have two cuts which I needed plastic surgery for.
Upsound Jean JansenCAMA002 08:29.Well, after my experience I don't want to attend. I won't ever attend illegal racing anymore.

[transition]

21.V/O On the Sunday afternoon, we meet up with Officer Boswell and the Ghost Squad who have intel on an illegal event in Atlantis. 40 km from Cape Town, it’s a known hotspot where things sometimes turn violent. It's a multidisciplinary operation.


Upsound Govan 12:23 Please just put the music on zero. Yeah, yeah, sorry. Yeah, I heard that. That's cool. You think we're going to find a big crowd here?[ Normally there's big crowds over there.

Officer Boswell CAMA066712:36 Guys come from all over Cape Town normally to go to that location. They call that Mexico. [Govan] Are they speaking in code?

Officer Boswell CAMA066712:36 : Racing fraternity mentioning Mexico, you must know its Atlantis.it's an industrial area. but still there's still companies operating in that area and you have shift-workers in the area so that makes it also very dangerous when they do perform these these races.Most of the times we are outnumbered.

22V/O Unsure of what to expect, the team calls in a surveillance plane equipped with advanced detection systems.

[ surveillance visuals…maybe use glitch effect to make them interesting]

Officer Boswell CAMA066712:36: As soon as they see us in the area they will start to leave.

23.V/O It looks like the racers are making a run for it … Boswell moves in!

24 V/O By the time we arrive, they’ve already fled, leaving behind signs of spinning and drag races.

Upsound Govan : There is that city golf…They were just here obviously got tipped off

Link So the BMW seen by the eye in the sky has managed to get away, the only spinning vehicle left is this old nissan 1400, and it looks like these guys were having such a good time that the back wheels gave out and weren't able to make a get away, and that is what it is.. A cat and mouse game , and often the mouse gets away.

Short Upsound Upset community member: You guys are impounding and you didnt see the car spinning.You liars! Now they are taking everything away, making us blow into pipes.We will go to prison.

25V/O As the bakkie is towed away, tensions rise on and off camera [ might need to read fast]

Short Upsound Upset community member : Put up barriers for us, don't worry about this stuff, put up nice things, organize ambulances and such things, it's so plain and simple ,with all that money you collect for us.


26 V/O To steer racers away from the streets, the City of Cape Town is providing dedicated tracks like Killarney. They offer a safe and legal outlet for racing enthusiasts

[ can we get visuals of Govan at the track, for placement]


Upsound JP smith Sit down CAMA0630 30:57You do want to give them an outlet., doing these Street to Strip and Robot Racing events.racing to give people a legal space to go and conduct it so that when they say look I don't have another avenue I can say on Friday nights there is robot racing or street to strip you can go to,

25V/O But not everyone is embracing this initiative

Upsound Mikayla CAMA0764 05:01 People say the track is different than the streets, and which is entirely true. Really? Track, road, and street road, it's a different feel.6:26 With a track, for example, Killarney, the racers have to pay a fee, why do we have to pay to enjoy ourselves?

26 VO They race for money, bragging rights, and the thrill. Despite the Ghost Squad’s efforts, street racing continues… because for some, no risk is too great to satisfy their need for speed.

[end]

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Join us as we dive into Cape Town’s underground world of illegal street racing and the elite Ghost Squad’s relentless pursuit to bring these speedsters to justice.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This story highlights the daring operations of the Ghost Squad, a covert unit within Cape Town’s Metro Police, dedicated to curbing the rampant street racing epidemic that endangers lives. The squad's efforts showcase a crucial fight for public safety against a deeply embedded culture of speed.
metadata.Summary: Cape Town has become a hotspot for illegal street racing, a dangerous pastime that has led to countless accidents, fatalities, and a growing public safety concern. The Ghost Squad, an elite division of the Cape Town Metro Police, was formed to combat this threat. Operating with unmarked vehicles and covert tactics, the squad has become the frontline in a battle against street racers who show little regard for the law or human life. This episode will explore the origins of illegal street racing in Cape Town, delving into the thrill-seeking culture that drives it. We'll follow the Ghost Squad on their night patrols, capturing their high-adrenaline confrontations with racers and offering viewers an inside look at the challenges they face in maintaining order on the city’s roads.
metadata.Further information: Our story will unfold in two parts: the first will introduce viewers to the world of illegal street racing, featuring interviews with participants and community members impacted by this reckless behavior. The second part will focus on the Ghost Squad’s operations, showcasing their tactics, challenges, and successes in apprehending offenders. We will capture the intensity of street racing through real footage, reenactments, and first-hand accounts, contrasting it with the Ghost Squad’s dedication to restoring safety. The episode will also address the legal and social implications of street racing, questioning whether current measures are enough to curb the issue. We will reference past incidents of street racing tragedies, emphasizing the urgent need for continued law enforcement efforts. Interviews with traffic safety experts will provide insights into potential solutions, while community members will voice their concerns and hopes for safer streets. The episode will conclude with a reflection on the ongoing struggle between thrill-seekers and the forces of law and order.
